messages.author: 28a8cbaeb7718d07
messages.subject: case weights in Stan
parts: I have some data that go back into the past, and I would like to downweight old observations, say an exponentially weighted scheme that weights year-old observations half as much as current ones. Is there a way of handling that in Stan that has escaped my attention (likely!) As an example, say I have data that i believe to be Poisson with constant mean lambda, each observation having a date attached, but I would like to give more weight to recent observations as above?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] case weights in Stan
parts:
You just want to multiply the log likelihoods for each data point
directly by the weights and it'll be equivalent to having that many observations,
e.g., with parameter lambda > 0, observations y[n] >= 0, and weight[n] > 0,

for (n in 1:N)
increment_log_prob(weight[n] * poisson_log(y[n], lambda));

If all weight[n] == 1, this reduces to the usual case. Usually if you're doing
a regression instead of lambda, you'd want to use something like:

poisson_log_log(y[n], beta * x[n]);

which exponentiates the linear predictor (beta * x[n]).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] case weights in Stan
parts:
You might be better served with some kind of time series model
that lets parameters vary over time rather than using some kind
of ad-hoc weighting which won't predict all of your data well.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] case weights in Stan
parts:
Hi, I’ll play the “Andrew” role in this conversation and say that I don’t recommend this sort of weighting of likelihood factors, as it moves you away from a generative model. To put it another way, if lambda really is constant, it does not make sense to downweight old observations; and if lambda varies, you want to model that, to have lambda(t) which varies over time. Such a model will make more sense and have the effect of downweighting old observations.
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] case weights in Stan
parts: Thanks for the ideas. I agree with the points raised, that some kind of time-varying model would be the most descriptive. I have, ultimately, some kind of Bradley-Terry-like multivariate model in mind, but I wanted to get my head around something simpler first, hence my idea of a Poisson model with "slowly-varying" mean (whatever that means). I like the clarity of Andrew's point: if not time-varying, no need for weights, and if *is* time-varying, model that.
